clue.text: Notice man with a package, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a printed notice put up on a wall or board
someone who posts a parcel, read as 'one who posts'

explanation.surface: A notice about a delivery man carrying a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a playful coinage: one who posts things, like a sender of a package.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice is a bill or placard stuck up for display, and the playful second sense is a person who sends mail.

clue.text: Bible class quietly avoids part of speech for missionary, say

indicators.note: avoids means these letters are left out of the word

parts.note: a preposition is a part of speech such as in or on
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
RE is religious education, the British school subject

explanation.surface: A missionary studying grammar and Bible lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missionary' suggests church work; it is the sexual position.
explanation.definitionFit: The missionary is a well-known sexual posture, an example of the general term.

clue.text: This could create wet areas

indicators.note: could create signals that a new arrangement is made from these letters

explanation.surface: Something that might leave places soaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from the ocean spreads over land in floods and tides, wetting it.

clue.text: Detect end of democracy by clairvoyance

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception, a sixth sense such as clairvoyance

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Using psychic powers to sense the fall of democracy.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy something is to catch sight of or spot it.

clue.text: A writer with special attributes

parts.note: a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A writer endowed with exceptional qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attributes' looks like a noun, qualities of the writer, but it is the verb: credits to.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute something to someone is to credit it to them, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Personal recognition of new sales fears after upheaval

indicators.note: after an upheaval things are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A firm's fresh worries about sales once turmoil has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Recognising one's own self and nature is self-knowledge, the meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: Daughter, 12, gatecrashes parties with potential broadcasters

indicators.note: gatecrashes means getting inside uninvited

parts.note: raves are large dance parties
refers to the answer to 12 across, the US state

explanation.surface: A twelve-year-old girl crashing parties along with media types.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like the daughter's age but points to the answer at 12 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Electromagnetic signals of this kind carry broadcasts, so they are potential carriers of programmes.

clue.text: British fight over new Sunday roasts

indicators.note: over means on top of, in a down clue the first pieces come above the rest

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: A British family argument over the new Sunday roast dinners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roasts' looks like the noun from a Sunday lunch, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook meat until its surface darkens is to sear or crisp it, which is what roasting does.

clue.text: Regular bread sadly rising rather unevenly at the ends

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of sorrow, said sadly

indicators.note: at the ends takes the first and last letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A complaint about a loaf rising badly and unevenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses ALAS to SALA; the first and last letters of 'rather unevenly' are R and Y. 'bread' is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and regular money paid for work is pay or wages.

clue.text: Spam fan was regularly back in bog

indicators.note: back means the selected letters are then read in reverse order
regularly means taking every other letter of these words, here the even ones

explanation.surface: A fan of tinned Spam has gone back into a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of SPAMFANWAS, giving PMAWS, and 'back' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog is wet marshy ground, the same thing as a marsh or fen.

clue.text: Tosspot allows bad dancing!

definitions.note: read literally as a pot in which things are tossed

indicators.note: dancing letters jig about into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunkard lets people dance badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tosspot' is a drunkard in everyday British slang, but here it is read literally: a pot in which salad is tossed.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad is tossed in this serving vessel, so it is a pot for tossing, a punning reading of the slang term for a drunk.

clue.text: Two hurricanes demolished flood defence system

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down and rebuilt in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Two hurricanes have destroyed a coastal flood barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flood defence system' suggests sea walls; it is the curtain that keeps a bathroom floor dry.
explanation.definitionFit: This hanging sheet stops shower spray from flooding the bathroom, a jokey description of its purpose.

clue.text: Defrost what needs cooking

indicators.note: something that needs cooking is to be worked over, so the letters of the word what are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to defrost food that still needs to be cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: To defrost something is to let its ice melt, a direct synonym.

clue.text: One pursuing British island state

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the one follows the island

parts.note: IOW is the Isle of Wight, an island off England's south coast
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Someone chasing a British island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest.

clue.text: She has discovered barbiturates

indicators.note: discovered means the cover, the outer letters, is taken off

parts.note: barbiturates are sedative drugs, known in slang as downers

explanation.surface: A woman has found some barbiturates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She has' reads as the start of a sentence but is the definition: a woman who has something.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has or possesses something is its proprietor; she is one such holder.

clue.text: Wastrel let loose in banking sector

indicators.note: let loose means set free to scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: A spendthrift set free among the banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York street stands for the US financial industry as a whole, a metonym.

clue.text: Gaining weight for good, too old to impress

indicators.note: gaining signals one letter being taken on in place of another
for marks the swap: weight in place of good

parts.note: overage means beyond the permitted age

explanation.surface: Someone putting on weight for their own good is too old to impress anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: In OVERAGE the G (good) is swapped for W (weight).
explanation.definitionFit: To overawe someone is to impress them so much they are cowed, a strong form of impressing.

clue.text: A custom abroad

parts.note: a way, as in 'the ways of the people', is a custom or habit

explanation.surface: A tradition found in another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is abroad is out of the country, gone from home.

clue.text: Anxious with truck not starting in middle of night

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: lorry is the British word for a truck

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: Fretting because the truck won't start in the middle of the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anxious and fretful is a state of concern, which this adjective describes.

clue.text: Put away TV when I date Marie (at last!)

parts.note: a TV is a television set
as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: Switching off the television to go on a date with Marie at long last.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something away is to reserve it or save it for later, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Look after book about the EU?

indicators.note: after means the look comes behind the book

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone reading up on the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' looks like the phrase meaning care for, but 'after' just places LO behind B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations allied by treaty; the European Union is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Offensive construction I noticed in report

indicators.note: in report signals that the phrase is heard, as spoken, rather than written

parts.note: I noticed is put as 'I saw'

explanation.surface: Someone reporting that they noticed an ugly building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I saw' spoken with a non-rhotic British accent sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly building that spoils the view is the classic example of a sight that offends the eye.

clue.text: Persuades politician coming in to restore cuts in U-turn

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the politician goes inside
in U-turn means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let the deleted text stand
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician performing a U-turn by reversing spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Political 'cuts' are budget cuts, but here they are cut text an editor puts back.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to entice or coax them, a near synonym.

clue.text: Wonderful day with client, essentially drinking French wine

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the wine goes inside
essentially picks the central letters, the essence of the word

parts.note: vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A splendid day spent with a client sipping French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes IE from the middle of 'client', which then holds VIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine is used colloquially to mean heavenly, excellent or delightful.

clue.text: To be old is to have time

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: A philosophical saying: being old means having lots of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To be, in the philosophical sense, is simply to have being or live.

clue.text: Last of Limburger I'm scared to smell

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the cheese's name

parts.note: eek is a cry of fright

explanation.surface: Someone frightened at the prospect of sniffing a famously pungent cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Limburger is a Belgian cheese notorious for its strong odour.
explanation.definitionFit: To reek is to give off a strong unpleasant odour, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Theresa really does hold ground

indicators.note: does hold means the words contain the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A politician named Theresa standing her ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of ground is a region or tract of land, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Encephalograph can provide indication of light-headedness, possibly

indicators.note: can provide means the long word yields the letters from within itself

explanation.surface: A brain scan might show dizziness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light-headedness' suggests dizziness; it is literally a head surrounded by light.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint's nimbus is a ring of light around the head, a literal reading of the phrase.

clue.text: Costs of new trade agreement described by sanctimonious prudes

indicators.note: described by means drawn around, so the prudes enclose the agreement

parts.note: prigs are self-righteous, priggish people
CETA is the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement between the EU and Canada

explanation.surface: Pious killjoys criticising a trade deal's expenses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Costs' looks like a verb but is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Labels showing what goods sell for state their costs, so the plural label stands for the prices.

clue.text: Excuse any ludicrous in-fighting by incompetent leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Pleas for silly infighting by incompetent bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used loosely to mean any excuse.

clue.text: Glowing women in dinner arrangement?

indicators.note: in places the women inside the seating

parts.note: a seating plan is how guests are arranged at dinner

explanation.surface: Women radiant at a dinner table plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The old saying goes: horses sweat, men perspire, ladies merely glow.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing is the polite euphemism for perspiring, especially said of women.

clue.text: Dutch maybe seen among getting-it-on guests?

indicators.note: seen among means the letters are found inside these words

explanation.surface: The setter Dutch spotted among amorous partygoers.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch is also the setter's pseudonym, so it looks like a name rather than a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch is a language, and a language is often called a mother tongue.
